date.as_written: śambho rāri śārādharādharārākātithau mitraje | māse māghamaghe ca śobhanayute kuṃbhe ca siṃhe ʼrjune
date.nakshatra_yoga: Maghā nakṣatra; Śobhana yoga; Sun in Kumbha, Moon in Siṃha; 'arjune' unclear

notes: The date is in verse. Rākā-tithi means the full moon of Māgha, and that fits Maghā nakṣatra and the Moon in Leo. 'Mitraje' most likely means Saturday (son of Mitra = Śani). The year chronogram 'śambho rāri śārādharādharā' is corrupt. Possible number-words include śambhu = 11, ari = 6, śara = 5, dharā = 1 and dharādhara = 7, but the word division is unclear, so no year or era can be fixed. The Newari script suggests NS. 'arjune' may stand for a planet or a corrupt word. In the second half, 'hantā dānava... prādā, siṃhā...' (slayer of the demon, [Pra]hlāda?, siṃha) may be a riddle that encodes the scribe's name, possibly Narasiṃha. This is speculative and not entered as a person. The scribe is otherwise only called 'asau ... mahadbuddhimān', who wrote ('lekhe' (!)) the Bhūtaḍāmara. The rest is stock scribal verses (pustakalikhanapariśrama..., urasi phaṇipatiḥ...).
